source.title: Why Heavy-Tailed Weight Spectra Predict Model Quality
source.authors: Joseph Wilson; C. van der Heide; Liam Hodgkinson; Zhi-Chao Wang; Fred Roosta; Michael W. Mahoney

record.file_problem: Full text is supplied; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: Measures correlations between trained-weight spectral properties and test error during natural- and permuted-label training, and reports how those relations vary by model, dataset, and training stage.
record.gate_note: The paper tests trained-weight measures against model quality, including during training and on a permuted-label task. It does not test the architecture, optimizer, batch-size, explicit-regularization, or model-size comparisons in the claim versions. Cited prior work is not extracted as this study’s result. The reported correlations and fitted spectral-parameter results are included below.
record.test_reason: The study tests spectral predictors of test performance, not any listed claim version. BFE-W is neither magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness nor a measurement of the training–test gap in V7. The permuted-label experiment reports 99% training accuracy, but does not establish V1's paired natural-label and random-label held-out accuracies with the same architecture and recipe.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that weight-based Bayes free energy predicts model quality in several CV and language-model settings, and connect training dynamics to fitted HTMP parameters. They acknowledge failures for dropout and vision-transformer models, post-hoc λ tuning for CV trajectories, and limitations of derivations restricted to regression and final-layer weights.
record.recipe_differences: This study measures spectral/free-energy predictors of model quality rather than directly comparing the claim’s listed training interventions or magnitude-aware sharpness. Its ResNet experiments use SGD, momentum 0.9, batch size 100, weight decay 0.0001, no augmentation, and no dropout; the permuted-label study trains ResNet18 on CIFAR-10 with randomly permuted labels.
record.method_sensitivity: BFE-W correlations vary by model class and weight matrix; dropout before final-layer weights and vision transformers do not show good correlation. For CV training trajectories, λ set separately at each epoch gives poor correlation, while fixing λ at the test-error-minimizing epoch works best. Pythia models use different training steps and weight matrices; QueryKey correlations are mixed and Pythia-12B QueryKey weights are strongly anti-correlated across most layers.

fits_no_version.finding: BFE-W correlates with held-out performance across several pretrained model suites and training trajectories, with dependence on λ, model family, and weight matrix.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-based Bayes free energy can predict held-out performance in some model families and training regimes.

fits_no_version.finding: CV test-error minima align with an optimal fitted HTMP ratio; Pythia performance improves as κ increases after the ratio approaches its optimum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fitted HTMP spectral parameters track distinct aspects of CV and language-model training dynamics.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026, 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems
record.problems: The paper’s main BFE-W derivation is for final-layer weights and regression; it applies the measure to deeper weights with motivation in Appendix F.2. For CV training, λ is tuned post hoc using the epoch with minimum test error. Dropout and vision-transformer model classes show poor correlation. Some results are described from figures without numerical values in the supplied text; the paper shows mean and 95% CI in figures but does not give CI values in text. The paper’s spectral predictor correlations do not directly measure training-to-test error gaps or the magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness in V7.
record.rows_left_out: No results over the 60-row cap; all extracted results retained. Cited prior-work findings and purely theoretical derivations are not rows.

untested.parts: Coexistence under the same architecture and recipe, including natural-label held-out accuracy above chance and random-label held-out accuracy at chance. Random-label training fit alone is reported.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected generalization comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under specified tuning budgets and recovery recipes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Effects of adding or removing dropout on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with training–test gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All corrected states describe whether the rows establish a listed version, not whether their spectral findings occurred. The supplied text links reproduction code, so the record's code-release field should not say 'not stated'.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare random-label and natural-label held-out accuracy or test the listed architectures and random-label fit conditions; it reports a permuted-label training experiment on ResNet18.
Does not compare magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness against norm- and margin-based measures; it evaluates free energy and HTMP spectral parameters, not the V7 sharpness measure.

rows.check: Spectral free energy versus test accuracy does not measure V7's sharpness–generalization-gap relationship.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 with randomly permuted training labels
rows.operation_detail: Tracked BFE-W against test cross-entropy during training using the third-layer convolutional weight.
rows.measure: Correlation of BFE-W with test error
rows.note: The paper states the free energy predicts test error closely once constrained to interpolating epochs.
rows.check: The measured correlation tests the spectral predictor, not V7 or V1's coexistence claim. H.1 reports ρ=0.819 for Figure 6 top right without explicitly restricting that coefficient to interpolating epochs; the subsequent interpolation-restricted claim is qualitative.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 with randomly permuted training labels
rows.operation_detail: Compared test cross-entropy and BFE-W with fitted HTMP ratio h=κ/β during interpolating epochs.
rows.measure: Whether the model with ratio closest to h* is optimal
rows.value: The optimal model corresponds to the interpolating model whose h is closest to h*
rows.note: Authors say the task has no feature learning and Bayes optimal accuracy is 10%.
rows.check: The spectral optimum on permuted labels does not establish V1's paired held-out accuracy results or measure V7 sharpness. The stated 10% accuracy is a theoretical chance benchmark, not measured test accuracy.

rows.check: Spectral-ratio changes during overfitting do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness.

rows.subject: Vision transformer models
rows.operation_detail: Compared BFE-W with top-5 ImageNet test accuracy for vision transformer models.
rows.measure: Spearman correlation of BFE-W with top-5 test accuracy
rows.value: Combined ρ = 0.14; Swin ρ = −0.83; ViT ρ = 0.20
rows.note: Paper states vision transformers do not show good correlation.
rows.check: Transformer spectral correlations do not test V7. The pooled value also hides a negative Swin correlation and positive ViT correlation.

rows.subject: Dropout models (EfficientNet, MNASNet, MobileNet, and VGG)
rows.operation_detail: Compared BFE-W with top-5 ImageNet test accuracy for models using dropout before final-layer weights.
rows.measure: Spearman correlation of BFE-W with top-5 test accuracy
rows.value: Combined ρ = 0.00
rows.note: The study attributes lack of correlation as possibly related to dropout before the final-layer weights.
rows.check: Spectral prediction among models using dropout tests neither V7 nor dropout's effect on test error in V6; there is no matched dropout intervention.

rows.subject: ResNet, VGG, and DenseNet legacy models
rows.stage_stated: legacy ImageNet checkpoints used in Martin et al. (2021)
rows.operation_detail: Compared BFE-W and HT-SR metrics with top-5 ImageNet test accuracy.
rows.measure: BFE-W Spearman correlation with test accuracy
rows.value: DenseNet −0.80; ResNet −0.90; VGG 0.81; Combined 0.48
rows.note: VGG uses dropout before final-layer weights; combined correlation has opposite direction from the non-dropout groups.
rows.check: Comparisons between spectral metrics do not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness ranking. The pooled correlation also combines opposite subgroup directions.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ImageNet torchvision combined pool; Pythia and Qwen3.5 model suites; ResNet50 and Pythia training trajectories; permuted-label ResNet18 interpolating epochs
reader_labels.reason: BFE-W or the fitted HTMP ratio tracks test quality in these settings (R1–R5, R7–R15). This is a related spectral/free-energy measure, not the magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness named in V7.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CV epoch tracking with epoch-specific λ; ResNet18/34 CIFAR-10 and Pythia 2.8B/6.9B training trajectories; deeper-layer Pythia measurements
reader_labels.reason: The relation depends on λ choice and model/weight setting, and some Pythia QueryKey results are mixed (R6, R15–R18).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Pythia-12B QueryKey matrices across most layers; vision transformers; dropout models; pooled legacy models including VGG
reader_labels.reason: The reported anti-correlation or absent/weak pooled relation does not consistently follow a claim that the measure tracks a smaller generalization gap (R19–R22).
